newsitem.title: PERU: Banco de Credito to issue $120 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Credito to issue $120 mln bonds.

text.p: Peru's largest bank, Banco de Credito, decided to make a subordinated bond issue worth up to $120 million, a Lima stock notice said Tuedsay.

The notice in the Lima bolsa's daily bulletin said Credito planned to issue the bonds in two tranches -- one in local currency for up to 150 million soles and the other in dollars for up to $60 million.
The bank has not announced the date nor the conditions for the issue, according to the notice.
Subordinated bonds permit the issuer to use proceeds to raise effective equity, equity and risk-weighted assets.
Banco de Credito is 90.1 percent-owned by Credicorp Ltd, a holding firm made up of shares of Credito, Peruvian insurer El Pacifico Peruano Suiza and offshore Atlantic Security Bank.
